title: Cowes factory reveals experimental 'flying saucer' airship - County Press archives
excerpt: The Isle of Wight County Press has been bringing the news to Islanders since 1884. We've delved into the archives to find out what was happening in days gone by.
content:
The Isle of Wight County Press has been bringing the news to Islanders since 1884. We've delved into the archives to find out what was happening in days gone by.

125 Years Ago

November 23, 1901

There was considerable relief at the arrival of the brigantine ship Rapid in Hartlepool, a week later than scheduled after its departure from Yarmouth. The Captain, H. S. Digby, reported “a most awful passage”, including dense fog and gale force winds.

Princess Henry of Battenberg, Governor of the Island, unveiled a plaque at Ryde Town Hall to commemorate local servicemen who took part in the South African campaign.

A private ball took place in Seaview to honour the coming of age of Mr J. Maudslay, youngest son of Mr and Mrs Maudslay of Worcester Lodge.

100 Years Ago

November 20, 1926

The newly-elected mayor of Newport was rung-in by the parish church bells, the ceremony having been postponed owing to illness in the neighbourhood of the church.

There was a well-attended whist drive and social organised in connection with the Royal British Legion. Including poppy-day and church collections, the total amount raised in St Helens for Earl Haig's fund was £30 13s. 6d.

75 Years Ago

November 24, 1951

Serious concerns were raised over flooding in the Cowes area, with heavy rainfall causing road subsidence and serious damage to houses in Church Path, East Cowes.

A confidential report, setting out the Island's case against the proposed closure of the railway system, was unanimously approved by the IW Chamber of Commerce.

The reduction in the foreign travel allowance to £50 meant the Island's tourist attractions were hoping and preparing for a busy season in 1952.

50 Years Ago

November 20, 1976

Somerton factory, Cowes, revealed an experimental prototype of a huge, ‘flying saucer’ airship, a transporter named Skyship.

The Island's ambulances answered only emergency calls for one day after drivers decided that two of the vehicles were “completely worn out”.

Concerns were raised at a public meeting that Cowes had lost its identity since local government merged the town into Medina borough.
